title: The canonical localization-algebra map is an equivariant E-theory K-homology isomorphism for proper cocompact isometric actions with separable coefficients
author: Christopher Wulff
difficulty_reason: The proof compares concrete finite-propagation localization operators with equivariant KK cycles and then identifies the resulting transformation with the canonical map to E-theory. It constructs the projection-valued representative of a localized unitary class and checks the coefficient-natural transformation on the identity cycle using an explicit zero-propagation projection. This verifies the particular asymptotic-morphism map, rather than merely asserting that the two groups are abstractly isomorphic.
source_version: Official SIGMA 18 (2022) article 057, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2022.057; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-09-30, exact bytes pinned by SHA256

proof_review.method: Published author proof/core and local context fidelity screening
proof_review.note: Select the absolute Theorem6.8 case with X a proper metric space, a countable discrete group Gamma acting properly, isometrically and cocompactly, and D a separable Gamma-C*-algebra. The canonical Delta is the specific composition defined on physical page54 from the localization asymptotic morphism delta, and K-homology is E_Gamma(C0(X),D) as defined on page53. The full author even-degree unitary/projection computation and the suspension passage to odd degree are included. The prior equivariant Paschke/localization isomorphisms [16 AppendixB] are explicitly background in this cocompact case; the author proves that their composition with this Delta is the canonical coefficient-natural KK-to-E isomorphism by checking the identity class. The newly modified noncocompact truncation argument, nonseparable direct-limit extension and relative five-lemma consequence are not selected. All relevant module/propagation and localization definitions are included.

statement_scope: Theorem6.8 absolute case only, with the added restrictions of a countable discrete group, proper cocompact isometric action and separable coefficient algebra D. Delta is exactly the page54 asymptotic-morphism map. Noncocompact, nonseparable and relative cases are contextual only.
